name: Fish Tank Stocking Calculator
seoTitle: Fish Tank Stocking Calculator — Formula & Results
seoDesc: Stocking is limited by filter capacity and by the space adult fish need, and both are usually miscalculated because people stock for the size the fish are now
summary:
Stocking is limited by filter capacity and by the space adult fish need, and both are usually miscalculated because people stock for the size the fish are now. It returns stocking capacity, stocking level, adult biomass and turnovers per hour, and the panel shows all of them at once.

This calculator gives the inch-per-gallon and surface-area limits, the biomass the filter must process and how many fish of each adult size fit. Every result is derived from the boxes you fill in, so changing one input updates the whole panel at once. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Fish Tank Stocking
sections.html:
Capacity (cm of adult fish) = volume (L) × turnover factor; biomass ≈ count × (length/10)³ × 10 g

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit

factorcm of fish per litrecm/L

sections.title: How do I use the Fish Tank Stocking?
sections.html:
The form asks only for what the formula needs — nothing is optional decoration.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: true water volume of 160 L, adult length of the species of 6 cm, fish planned of 20, filter turnover of 800 L/h, stocking factor of 1 cm per L.

Substituting them into the formula gives stocking capacity of 160 cm, stocking level of 75%, adult biomass of 43.2 g, turnovers per hour of 5 per hour, fish of this size that fit of 26.67 fish.

The arithmetic is the page's own: change one box and the result moves by the amount the formula implies, which is the quickest way to convince yourself the tool is honest.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
A raw figure only means something next to the bands it is normally judged against. Here is the scale that goes with this one:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
below 60%Understockedsafe, and the filter has headroom
60 – 90%Well stockedthe target for a display tank
90 – 110%At the limitonly with strong filtration and weekly changes
above 110%Overstockedammonia spikes, disease and stunted growth

  • The old inch-per-gallon rule is a volume proxy for oxygen demand and waste, which scale with mass, not length. It fails badly for deep-bodied fish, so the biomass line here is the more honest limit.

  • Freshwater community tanks: about 1 cm of adult fish per litre of net water; cichlids and goldfish need double the volume because they are taller and messier.

  • Filter turnover of five times the tank volume per hour is the usual starting point; the fish load is what actually decides whether it is enough.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
The arithmetic is simple; the inputs are where things go wrong. The usual culprits:

  • Stocking by the size of the juveniles you bought.
  • Ignoring that fish grow: 20 small tetras and 20 silver dollars are not the same tank.
  • Adding all the fish at once, which overwhelms the bacteria before they multiply.

faq.q: How many fish can I keep in 100 L?
faq.a: Roughly 100 cm of adult fish at 1 cm per litre — so about 16 fish of 6 cm, or 8 of 12 cm.

faq.q: Does more filtration allow more fish?
faq.a: It buys some headroom, but oxygen and swimming space set a hard ceiling.

faq.q: What does the Fish Tank Stocking actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns stocking capacity, stocking level, adult biomass and turnovers per hour. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
